content: Seasonal index (ratio-to-moving-average) in SQL: Step 1 = GROUP BY (brand, month_number), SUM(qty)/COUNT(months) as avg_month_qty. Step 2 = overall average across all months for bucket = SUM(all_qty)/(12.0 * years). Step 3 = seasonal_factor = avg_month_qty / overall_avg. Factor=1.0 means no seasonality; >1 = peak; <1 = trough. PostgreSQL: SELECT brand, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM data_pedido::date) AS mes, SUM(quantidade) AS total, SUM(SUM(quantidade)) OVER (PARTITION BY brand) / 12.0 AS anual_media, SUM(quantidade) / (SUM(SUM(quantidade)) OVER (PARTITION BY brand) / 12.0) AS fator. Minimum history threshold: need at least 12 months of data (1 full year) in the bucket for the factor to be meaningful. With <12 months, fator=1.0 (fallback). CLAMP the factor between 0.3 and 3.0 to avoid extreme outliers.
